country: multiple (three ICU cohorts: MIMIC-IV, HIRID, PPICU)

links.outcome: Cross-hospital transfer performance drop of ICU prediction models using LLM-based portable embeddings versus baselines
links.effect: LLM-summary embeddings were competitive in-distribution and showed smaller relative performance drops when transferring to new hospitals, so performance degradation at new sites still occurs but is reduced.
links.quote: Across three cohorts (MIMIC-IV, HIRID, PPICU), on multiple clinically grounded forecasting and classification tasks, we find that our approach is simple, easy to use and competitive with in-distribution with grid imputation, self-supervised representation learning, and time series foundation models, while exhibiting smaller relative performance drops when transferring to new hospitals.

unlisted_practices: Using frozen LLM-generated text summaries plus frozen text embeddings as portable patient representations to reduce retraining across hospitals
Using structured prompts to reduce variance of downstream predictors
Testing demographic recoverability (age, sex) from embeddings as a privacy check

screen.reason: Evaluates using LLM-generated portable representations to address cross-hospital distribution shifts and evaluates structured prompt design to reduce predictive model variance.

primary.practice: structured prompt design for representation stability and privacy/cross-site transfer evaluation
